summary: Verified from primary sources on 2026-09-13. (1) LICENSE.md as shipped in timm/vit_large_patch16_dinov3.lvd1689m, facebook/dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m and facebook/dinov3-vit7b16-pretrain-lvd1689m is word-identical, carries "Last Updated: August 19, 2025", and its redistribution clause 1.b.i ends "...you may only do so under the terms of this Agreement and you shall provide a copy of this Agreement with any such DINO Materials." — the string "Built with DINOv3"/"prominently display" occurs 0 times. Only the ai.meta.com web page (dated "August 14, 2025") has the (A)/(B) clause with "prominently display “Built with DINOv3”". GitHub history shows the shipped file NEVER had that clause: the Aug-14 initial import (11c58638) already lacked it, and the Aug-19 commit ffb4bb89 "Fix incorrect references to other sections (#76)" changed only the date and "Sections 5, 6 and 9" -> "Sections 3, 4 and 7". So the divergence is web-page-vs-shipped-file, not a dated revision. (2) arXiv 2508.10104 is still v1 (13 Aug 2025); Table 14 contains NO ViT-7B row (only S/S+/B/L/H+ students vs DINOv2/SigLIP 2/PEcore). ViT-L row: IN-ReaL 90.2, IN-R 88.1, Obj. 74.8, Ox.-H 63.1, ADE20k 54.9, NYU 0.352, DAVIS 79.9, NAVI 62.3, SPair 61.2; ViT-H+ row: 90.3, 90.0, 78.6, 64.5, 54.8, 0.352, 79.3, 63.3, 56.3 (PDF pdftotext and arXiv HTML agree cell-for-cell). The 7B teacher's numbers live in Tables 3/4/5/7: ADE20k 55.9, NYUv2 0.309, NAVI 64.4, SPair 58.7, DAVIS 71.1/79.7/83.3 (S/M/L, M = short side 960 for /16), ObjectNet 79.0. The "close to" sentence is in Sec. 1: "Notably, the efficient and widely adopted ViT-L model achieves performance close to that of the original 7B teacher across a variety of tasks." The frozen-protocol sentence opens Sec. 6: "Throughout our experiments, unless otherwise specified, we keep DINOv3 frozen and solely use its representations. We demonstrate that with DINOv3, finetuning is not necessary to obtain strong performance." (3) The 7B model card's Downstream Use paragraph reads verbatim: "While fine-tuning the models can yield some gains, it is recommended to keep this option as a last resort: the frozen features are expected to provide good performance out-of-the-box." (identical on the vitl16 card). Practical extra: the facebook/* repos are gated ("manual", contact-info form: name/DOB/country/affiliation/job title); the timm/* repos are NOT gated (model.safetensors HTTP 200 unauthenticated for L, H+, 7B) but carry the same dinov3-license. claims.claim: The LICENSE.md shipped in all three HF repos (timm/vit_large_patch16_dinov3.lvd1689m; facebook/dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m; facebook/dinov3-vit7b16-pretrain-lvd1689m) is word-identical, headed "*Last Updated: August 19, 2025*", and does NOT contain "Built with DINOv3" or "prominently display" (0 occurrences). Section 1.b.i verbatim: "i. Distribution of DINO Materials, and any derivative works thereof, are subject to the terms of this Agreement. If you distribute or make the DINO Materials, or any derivative works thereof, available to a third party, you may only do so under the terms of this Agreement and you shall provide a copy of this Agreement with any such DINO Materials." Section 1.b.ii: "If you submit for publication the results of research you perform on, using, or otherwise in connection with DINO Materials, you must acknowledge the use of DINO Materials in your publication." Section 1.b.v also bars use "for any activities subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) or end uses prohibited by Trade Controls, including those related to military or warfare purposes". The timm copy is byte-identical (sha256 25d122eb8f5b880fd23c736fb6ea8018ee45c12237e00b8a86d14c653904999e) to GitHub facebookresearch/dinov3/LICENSE.md; the two gated facebook/ copies were read from the rendered blob pages (word-diff vs timm: only tag-stripping artefacts). By contrast the ai.meta.com page (canonical https://ai.meta.com/resources/models-and-libraries/dinov3-license/, header "DINOv3 License August 14, 2025") reads: "...you may only do so under the terms of this Agreement. You shall (A) provide a copy of this Agreement with any such DINO Materials; and (B) prominently display “Built with DINOv3” on a related website, user interface, blogpost, about page, or product documentation." and its survival clause says "Sections 5, 6 and 9 shall survive" (the shipped file: "Sections 3, 4 and 7"). GitHub history: initial import 11c58638 (2025-08-14T15:40Z) already read "Last Updated: August 14, 2025" with 0 occurrences of "Built with"; commit ffb4bb89 (2025-08-19T08:56Z, "Fix incorrect references to other sections (#76)") changed only the date line and the survival-clause numbers. So the shipped file never carried the "Built with DINOv3" obligation at any date; the (B) clause exists only on Meta's web page.

claims.why_it_matters_here: Determines the compliance burden if a DINOv3-encoded policy checkpoint or code is redistributed (e.g. pushed to the repo or shared): under the shipped Aug-19 file only a copy of the Agreement + publication acknowledgement are required; the "Built with DINOv3" display obligation exists only on Meta's web page, so the orchestrator should cite the shipped LICENSE.md text, not the ai.meta.com text, and flag the ITAR/military-use clause for an ROV project.

claims.claim: arXiv 2508.10104 is still v1 ("arXiv:2508.10104v1 [cs.CV] 13 Aug 2025"; PDF and HTML identical). Table 14 has NO ViT-7B row — it lists only the distilled students S/S+/B/L/H+ against DINOv2/SigLIP 2/PEcore. Caption verbatim: "Table 14: Comparison of our family of models against open-source alternatives of comparable size. We showcase our ViT-{S, S+, B, L, H+} models on a representative set of global and dense benchmarks: classification (IN-ReAL, IN-R, ObjectNet), retrieval (Oxford-H), segmentation (ADE20k), depth (NYU), tracking (DAVIS at 960px), and keypoint matching (NAVI, SPair). We match the number of patch tokens for a fair comparison across models of different patch size." Rows (IN-ReaL | IN-R | Obj. | Ox.-H | ADE20k | NYU↓ | DAVIS | NAVI | SPair): L DINOv3 = 90.2 | 88.1 | 74.8 | 63.1 | 54.9 | 0.352 | 79.9 | 62.3 | 61.2; H+ DINOv3 = 90.3 | 90.0 | 78.6 | 64.5 | 54.8 | 0.352 | 79.3 | 63.3 | 56.3; (for reference L DINOv2 = 89.7 | 79.1 | 64.7 | 55.7 | 48.8 | 0.394 | 73.4 | 59.9 | 57.0). The 7B teacher's numbers on the same benchmarks come from the main-body tables (all frozen backbone; Tables 3 and 7 state 1024 patch tokens = 512×512 for /16): Table 3 ADE20k 55.9, NYUv2 RMSE 0.309; Table 4 NAVI 64.4, SPair 58.7; Table 5 DAVIS J&F 71.1/79.7/83.3 at S/M/L (M = video short side 960 px for patch-16, matching Table 14's "DAVIS at 960px"); Table 7 ObjectNet 79.0. Cross-table deltas ViT-L minus 7B (my computation, not the paper's): ADE20k −1.0 mIoU, NYU +0.043 RMSE (≈14 % worse), DAVIS@960 +0.2 (L ≥ 7B), NAVI −2.1, SPair +2.5 (L beats both 7B and H+), ObjectNet −4.2. Fig. 16(a) sizes: ViT-L 300M params, 163/721 GFLOPs at 256/512 px; ViT-H+ 840M, 450/1903; ViT-7B 6716M, 3550/14515.

claims.why_it_matters_here: The size recommendation cannot cite "Table 14 ViT-L vs 7B" because the 7B is not in that table; it must cite Table 14 (L, H+) plus Tables 3/4/5/7 (7B), with the caveat that the comparison is cross-table. The numbers themselves support the recommendation: ViT-L is within ~1 mIoU (ADE20k) and ~2 points (NAVI) of the 7B and ahead on DAVIS@960 and SPair, while H+ adds nothing on the dense columns (ADE20k 54.8 vs 54.9, NYU 0.352 vs 0.352, DAVIS 79.3 vs 79.9, SPair 56.3 vs 61.2) for 2.8× the params and 2.6× the FLOPs — the relevant axis for a 3-channel depth-encoding observation is the dense columns, not IN-R/ObjectNet where H+ leads.

claims.claim: Exact sentences from arXiv 2508.10104v1. Sec. 1 (Introduction, "The DINOv3 Family of Models"): "Notably, the efficient and widely adopted ViT-L model achieves performance close to that of the original 7B teacher across a variety of tasks." Fig. 16 caption: "(b) We compare DINOv3 ViT-H+ to its 7B-sized teacher; despite having almost 10× less parameters, the ViT-H+ is close to DINOv3 7B in performance." Sec. 7.1 body: "To this end, we run a comparison of our largest ViT-H+ with the 7B teacher. As shown in Fig. 16b, the largest student achieves performance that is on par with the 8 times larger ViT-7B model." and "The strength of larger models can be successfully distilled into more efficient, smaller models with little or no loss of quality." Frozen-evaluation protocol, opening of Sec. 6 Results: "In this section, we evaluate our flagship DINOv3 7B model on a variety of computer vision tasks. Throughout our experiments, unless otherwise specified, we keep DINOv3 frozen and solely use its representations. We demonstrate that with DINOv3, finetuning is not necessary to obtain strong performance." Sec. 7.1 protocol: "For a fair comparison, we ensure that the input sequence length is equivalent across models. Specifically, for model with a patch size of 16 we input images of size 512 × 512 versus 448 × 448 when models are using patch size 14." Note the ViT-L "close to" claim is a qualitative intro statement; the paper's only quantitative student-vs-teacher comparison is Fig. 16b (H+ vs 7B bar chart on IN1k/Obj./ReAL/ADE20k/Citysc.), not a ViT-L-vs-7B table.
sources: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2508.10104 (pdftotext lines 186-191 intro sentence; 940-943 Sec. 6 frozen protocol; 1603-1605 Sec. 7.1 protocol; 1689-1692 Fig. 16 caption; 1719-1722 and 1749-1752 Sec. 7.1 body)
claims.why_it_matters_here: These are the literal sentences the recommendation quotes. The orchestrator should quote the ViT-L sentence as the authors' qualitative claim and back it with the Table 14 vs Tables 3/4/5/7 numbers (claim 2), and should note that all paper evidence is for a FROZEN backbone at 512 px / 1024 tokens — the project fine-tunes the encoder (lr 3e-5, EMA) at 224 px / 196 patch tokens on ~75 episodes, a regime the paper does not evaluate.

claims.claim: The facebook/dinov3-vit7b16-pretrain-lvd1689m model card (rendered page, canonical https://huggingface.co/facebook/dinov3-vit7b16-pretrain-lvd1689m) states under "Uses": "The models are vision backbones providing multi-purpose features for downstream tasks." — "Direct Use: The models can be used without fine-tuning, with downstream classifiers as simple as linear layers, to obtain competitive results: on image classification, using k-NN classifiers on the class token; on image classification, with logistic regression classifiers applied on the class token; on image classification, with a linear layer applied on the class token and the average of the patch tokens; on image retrieval using nearest neighbors; on geometric and semantic 3D keypoint correspondances; on depth estimation, semantic segmentation, using linear layers; on unsupervised object discovery; on video segmentation tracking; on video classification, using a small 4-layer attentive probe" — "Downstream Use: While fine-tuning the models can yield some gains, it is recommended to keep this option as a last resort: the frozen features are expected to provide good performance out-of-the-box." The identical Downstream Use paragraph appears on the vitl16 card. Model Details on the same card: "For a 224x224 image, this results in 1 class token + 4 register tokens + 196 patch tokens = 201 tokens" and "12 models are provided: ... 1 ViT-7B trained from scratch, 5 ViT-S/S+/B/L/H+ models distilled from the ViT-7B, 4 ConvNeXt-{T/S/B/L} models distilled from the ViT-7B". Access: HF API reports gated="manual" for both facebook/ repos (form: First/Last Name, Date of birth, Country, Affiliation, Job title; page text "You need to agree to share your contact information to access this model"), lastModified 2025-08-19T09:00Z; the timm/ mirrors (vit_large / vit_huge_plus / vit_7b _patch16_dinov3.lvd1689m) report gated=False and model.safetensors returns HTTP 200 unauthenticated, under the same license_name "dinov3-license" (timm L lastModified 2025-09-24T22:44Z).
sources: https://huggingface.co/facebook/dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m (rendered model card, same Downstream Use paragraph)
claims.why_it_matters_here: Meta's own guidance is frozen-first / fine-tune as "last resort", which argues against the project's current encoder-fine-tuning default (lr 3e-5, EMA, 75 episodes) for a 7B or H+ backbone and supports a frozen-ViT-L-features (or low-lr / partial) first experiment. The timm mirrors being ungated but same-licensed means the deploy env (timm 1.0.29) can pull weights without the Meta form, but the license obligations (copy of Agreement on redistribution, publication acknowledgement, ITAR clause) still attach.

gaps: ai.meta.com/resources/models-and-libraries/dinov3-license/ returns HTTP 400 to curl and Wayback snapshots are JS-rendered; the verbatim Aug-14 text was taken from a sibling agent's scratchpad capture (meta_lic.html, canonical tag verified, fetched 2026-09-13 22:48) and corroborated by a WebFetch summary — not from a fresh raw fetch by this agent.

The facebook/ LICENSE.md files could not be fetched raw (401 gated); text was taken from HF's rendered blob pages, which strip the `<ins>` markup — word content verified identical to the timm/GitHub file, byte identity not verifiable without accepting the gate.

The ViT-L-vs-7B numeric comparison is cross-table (Table 14 vs Tables 3/4/5/7). Both are frozen-backbone, and Tables 3/7 state 1024 patch tokens (512 px for /16) while Table 14 says only 'we match the number of patch tokens' and 'DAVIS at 960px'; the ObjectNet protocol in Table 14 (linear probe on IN1k, per Table 7) is inferred, not stated in the Table 14 caption.

The paper reports no experiment with (a) a 3-channel depth encoding as input, (b) 224 px / 196 tokens, or (c) fine-tuning the backbone on ~75 episodes; the 'close to the 7B teacher' claim is for frozen features at 512 px on natural RGB images.
arXiv version checked is v1 (13 Aug 2025); no later revision existed on 2026-09-13, but a future revision could add a 7B row to Table 14.
